newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-VENUS WILLIAMS WINS LIPTON MATCH INTERRUPTED BY RAT.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-VENUS WILLIAMS WINS LIPTON MATCH INTERRUPTED BY RAT.

text.p: Venus Williams outlasted fellow American Ginger Helgeson Nielsen 6-1 4-6 6-3 in a first-round match at the Lipton Championships Thursday that saw a 20-minute rat delay.
The 110th-ranked Williams had just lost her serve in the opening game of the second set when the rotund rodent started a mad dash through the stands and around the spectators' seats.
The jumpy fans created quite a scene, nervously looking around to see where the rat would turn up next. Eventually, the animal was caught in a cardboard box, and play resumed.

"That was very odd," Williams said of the vermin experience. "I really didn't know what was going on. Actually, I thought it was some type of creature. I guess I figured it was rat. I thought it was some type of mouse, not a rat. A full-blown rat?"
It was a day when a number of teenagers, including the 16-year-old Williams, were seen in first-round action.
Among the young upstarts to advance was 90th-ranked Anna Kournikova of Russia. The 15-year-old Kournikova breezed past 84th-ranked Nana Miyagi of Japn 6-2 6-0 in 47-minutes.
Two 19-year-olds also moved into the second round.
The 74th-ranked Annabel Ellwood of Australia posted a quick 6-2 6-1 victory over 64th-ranked Denisa Chladkova of the Czech Republic.
On the men's side, 101st-ranked Nicolas Kiefer, a wildcard recipient at the Lipton, won a hardfought 6-2 5-7 7-6 (7-3) victory over 95th-ranked Dennis van Scheppingern of the Netherlands.
Highly touted 20-year-old American Justin Gimelstob was on the losing side of the first round. The 143rd-ranked Gimelstob fell 7-6 (8-6) 3-6 6-4 to 120th-ranked Marcelo Charpentier of Argentina.

Williams tends to play matches where there are a lot of service breaks and unforced errors, and she made no exception against Helgeson Nielsen, who once ranked as high as 29th in the world but now is only 526th after suffering a right wrist injury that kept her off the tour for most of 1995 and 1996.
Overall, there were 13 service breaks in the match, with Williams successful on eight of her 14 break attempts and Helgeson Nielsen winning five of her eight.
In the 171-point match, 102 of the points were unforced errors. Williams made 50 blunders, while her opponent had 52.
Last week Williams reached the quarter-finals of the Evert Cup, the first tournament on her 1997 schedule. She lost an exciting three-set encounter with American Lindsay Davenport.

Williams said that on Friday, when the other players at The Lipton would be busy practicing or playing matches or hanging out at the courts, she would be sitting in a classroom at the nearby private school she attends.

"I have like nine geometry assignments," Williams moaned. "I have chemistry. I'm taking some college courses. I haven't written a report that was due today. That's what happens when you go to tournaments."
